_comment: Empirical bounds for the generative-background engine's 8 static orientation/scale/framing overrides (createGenerativeBackground() opts.rotationX/Y/Z, scaleX/Y/Z, offsetX/Y — src/shared/effects/webgl/generative-background.js). Measured, not guessed: silhouette-mode (u_silhouetteDebug) painted-coverage swept across each parameter in isolation, full-canvas, at effective phase 1.10 (u_time=27500), via scripts/generative-background/sweep-position-ranges.mjs. A value counts as 'still reads as an intentional folded form' when its coverage stays at or above ~30% of the baseline (all-default) coverage of 33.8% — below that the ribbon has rotated too edge-on, shrunk too far, or panned off-frame to read as anything but a thin sliver or nothing. Raw sweep data + full per-value table: scripts/generative-background/runs/sweep-1788779528746/. Step values are slider granularity choices, not measured.

rotationZ._comment: Tightened from the raw measured OK range (-180..180) — coverage at both extremes measured only 32% of baseline (10.7% absolute, right at the acceptance floor), so +/-150 keeps a safety margin rather than shipping a slider whose very ends are borderline-degenerate.

scaleY._comment: 0.1 and 0.25 both measured OUT (10% and 23% of baseline) — the ribbon flattens to a near-invisible line on this axis well before scaleX/scaleZ show the same effect, because scaleY compresses the fold's own stand-up axis.

offsetX._comment: Asymmetric by measurement, not a mistake — the default framing already sits off-centre (layer 2's own preset composition), so the object reaches the frame edge sooner in +X than -X. +800 measured OUT (28% of baseline); +600 was the last OK value (52%).
